method: Opus 5 workflow annotator per PA from ffmpeg frame grabs; two independent verifier lenses per pitch (timing, scoreboard_identity) that both had to return and pass; then the Claude Code session built a review sheet per pitch (decision boundary frames, bug crops, continuity samples, release crops) and looked at it directly before marking a row verified.
limitations: Selected-frame AI review, not continuous playback or independent human inter-rater measurement. Release estimates have +/-0.15 s manual uncertainty. Same-game development data, not an independent benchmark.
starting_commit_meaning: Claim commit before PA33-40 (5th inning) annotation; candidates were created during this task.

issues: (a) Condition (2) fails at the claimed decision 3746.50: Megill is still stepping onto the rubber. At 3746.40, 3746.50 and 3746.60 his trailing screen-left foot is off the dirt behind him, heel up with the sole showing, and his torso is still turning from back-to-camera (No. 38 visible) into the side-on set. At 3746.75 the far foot is motion-blurred and sits higher than its planted position, so it is still sliding in. From 3747.00 on, both feet stay in the same planted position (checked in 4-6x feet crops at 3747.00, 3747.25, 3747.50 and 3747.90). The earliest valid grid frame is 3747.00, not 3746.50.

(c) The motion has already started at 3748.00: the glove has lifted off the chest and the far (left) knee is bending forward with the leg blurred as it rises. 3747.90 is the last set frame, and at 3748.10 the leg is clearly up. The claim that 3748.00 still shows him set is wrong; motion_start should be 3748.00, not 3748.25.

The cutaway part of the claim holds: 3746.00 and 3746.25 are the tight close-up of Albies next to the umpire, and the live centre-field shot returns by 3746.50. But the true earliest frame comes later because of the pitcher's feet, not the cutaway.
Identity is confirmed (1-0, P:76, 0 outs, bases empty, down-arrow 5, NYM 0 / ATL 2). Release 3749.25 +/- 0.15 is confirmed.

Decision frame 3746.50 is a live wide angle from a low outfield camera, not the usual high centre-field view. It clearly shows Megill on the rubber and the batter in the box, so condition (1) holds, but the annotator's note should name the camera angle.

No batter line is shown at 3746.50. The batter identity comes from '2. ALBIES 1-1', which slides in at 3748.25 (partly cut off, during the leg lift) and is fully readable at 3751.00. That matches how the annotator reported it.

Criterion (a): at 3746.75 condition (2) still fails. Megill's free foot is still coming down and sliding in behind the planted pivot shoe. In 10x crops the toe of that shoe sits clearly above the top of the pivot cleat at 3746.75. It drops and moves forward step by step: at 3746.77 it is about 1.5 raw px lower, at 3746.80 about 4 px lower and 2 px further forward, and at 3746.85 about 4.5 px lower, where it then stays steady through 3747.75. The pivot shoe does not move at all over 3746.75-3746.80, so camera zoom does not explain the shift. The shoe also looks ghosted and translucent at 3746.75 and 3746.77, which points to motion blur. The annotator's claim that the 3746.75, 3746.80, 3746.90 and 3747.00 foot crops are identical does not hold for 3746.75.
Motion-compensated pixel difference on the free-shoe patch agrees: 9.9 for 3746.75->3746.80 against 4.7 for 3746.80->3746.90 and 3.9 for 3746.90->3747.00.

The next grid frame, 3747.00, meets all four conditions: centre-field camera; Megill set on the rubber with both feet planted; Albies in the box facing him with the bat up; bug readable. The window holds through 3747.25, 3747.50 and 3747.75 (still, no break). Suggested decision 3747.00, with previous grid 3746.75 failing for pitcher_not_on_rubber_or_moving.
3746.25 is a cutaway close-up of Albies (fails condition 1) and at 3746.50 the free foot is clearly in the air, so criterion (b) does not apply.

3746.75 is a borderline frame. In an enlarged crop of the feet, the free shoe sits behind the pivot shoe but looks ghosted and translucent (motion blur), while at 3747.00 it is solid and planted. That supports the claim that condition (2) still fails at 3746.75, but the call rests on a few pixels.

rows.bug_text: NYM 0 / ATL 2 / bases empty / down-5 / 0 outs / 1-0 / MEGILL :08 P:76 (no batter line at 3747.00; "2. ALBIES 1-1" first visible at 3748.10)
rows.note: SNY full game. Bottom 5, Megill vs Albies; 1-0 count, bases empty, 0 outs. I re-grabbed the boundary at 0.05 s spacing and looked at 8x-14x crops of the feet. At 3746.50 Megill's free (screen-left) foot is plainly in the air, sole showing above the rubber, and at 3746.65/3746.70 it is still coming down and sliding in from the left. At the previously claimed decision frame 3746.75 condition (2) still fails: the free shoe has arrived behind the planted pivot shoe but is not yet at rest. Measuring the rightmost bright shoe pixel of the free shoe in the band y=550-570, its toe sits at x=477/479 at 3746.65/3746.70, x=486 at 3746.75, x=488 at 3746.80, and then exactly 488 at 3746.85, 3746.90 and 3746.95; the top edge of that shoe at column x=484 is y=563 at 3746.75 and y=566 from 3746.80 on, and at x=488 the shoe does not reach that column at all at 3746.75 while it is at y=569 from 3746.80 onward and stays there. So at 3746.75 the free foot is still about 2 px short and 3 px high of the settled position it reaches at 3746.80 and then holds frozen, and the frame also shows the ghosted, translucent look of motion blur; a control patch on the dirt/rubber and the planted pivot shoe both drift only about 1 px per frame downward from the camera's slow zoom, so the free-foot displacement is real motion, not zoom. I therefore agree with the verifier and move the decision to the next grid frame. At 3747.00 all four conditions hold: the live centre-field camera shows Megill set on the rubber with both feet planted and still, Albies in the box facing him with the bat up, and the bug readable as NYM 0 / ATL 2, three empty diamonds, two empty out circles, down-arrow 5, 1-0, MEGILL :08 P:76 (no batter line at this frame; '2. ALBIES 1-1' first appears in my samples at 3748.10). Continuity sampled at 3747.00, 3747.25, 3747.50, 3747.75, 3747.90 and 3748.00, maximum gap 0.25 s, with no step-off, pickoff, time-out, batter leaving the box, cutaway or white bug wipe. Motion start: at 3747.75 and 3747.90 he is still with both legs straight and together and the glove only rising to the chest, and at 3748.00 the free leg has swung forward with the knee bent and the leg blurred off the ground, full leg lift by 3748.10, so motion_start = 3748.00. Release bracket: at 3749.10 the throwing arm is cocked back behind him, at 3749.20 the hand is up by the head with the arm still bent and no ball visible, at 3749.25 the arm is extended forward and high toward the plate with the blurred hand at the end of the extension, and at 3749.30 the ball is clearly separated in flight in front of the MLB.tv batter silhouette (further toward the plate at 3749.40), so release = 3749.25. ffmpeg frame grabs; selected-frame review, not continuous playback. issues: Refute criterion (b): 3959.50 and 3959.75 s both meet all four v2 conditions. The shot there is a live high-home wide angle, not a replay or scenic cutaway. It is one continuous slow zoom-in from about 3954.5 s. The bug is live: the pitch clock ticks :10 at 3957, :09 at 3958, :08 at 3959 and :07 at 3959.5. In enlarged crops, Megill stands still at the rubber, with the rosin bag in the same spot relative to his feet as in the 3960 centre-field frame. Olson stands upright in the left-handed box, bat up, facing the mound. The bug is fully readable. So 3960.00 is not the earliest valid frame.

The annotator's reason for failing condition (1) (the pitcher is 'a few pixels' and the batter 'cannot be resolved') conflicts with project precedent. Committed rows in game_747139_timing.json already accept a live high-home wide angle with a slow zoom-in as a valid shot (Megill on the rubber, d'Arnaud in the box). The pa20_26 verification refuted an annotator who rejected the same kind of shot (2077.25 s vs 2076.75 s), treating the cut to the centre-field camera as only a camera change. Here the pitcher is about 40 px tall and the batter about 50 px in the 1280x720 frames, larger than in the accepted 1706.25 frame.

Searching backwards: at 3955.00 Olson is bent over at the plate (digging in or adjusting), so condition (3) fails. At 3956.00 he is still stepping in with the bat raised high and his body turned, which is ambiguous. At 3957.00 he is upright in the box facing the pitcher, and Megill is on the rubber with his head down (allowed). The earliest confirmed valid frame is 3957.00, and the true earliest grid frame is in (3956.00, 3957.00]. I did not sample 3956.25 to 3956.75 because the extra-frame budget was used up.

Continuity from 3957 is unbroken in my samples: 3957, 3958, 3958.5, 3959, 3959.25, 3959.5, 3959.75 (wide angle), then 3960, 3963 and 3965.75 (centre-field). No step-off, time-out, batter leaving the box, replay or white bug wipe was seen. The 3959.75 to 3960 cut is only a change between two valid live angles.

Timing-lens note, not an identity issue: 3959.75 is a different live camera, a high wide angle from behind home plate. It shows Megill on the mound and Olson at the plate, and its bug reads the same state. The cut to the centre-field camera happens between 3959.75 and 3960.00. Whether that high wide shot passes condition (1), which would move the decision earlier than 3960, is for the timing verifier to decide.

Condition (1) at 3955.75 depends on accepting the live high-home wide angle, which runs from about 3955 to 3959.75 and zooms in slowly. Megill and Olson are only about 30-40 px tall in it. Both are identifiable in 5-10x crops, but I cannot resolve Olson's head direction, so 'facing the pitcher' is judged from his upright posture in the box.

The session scan flagged '3960 no bug', but I could not reproduce it: the bug is fully readable at 3959.75, 3960.00 and 3960.25 (clock :07). The cut from the high-home angle to centre-field falls between 3959.75 and 3960.00 and was not sampled below 0.25 s, so a very brief white wipe at the cut cannot be strictly excluded. None is visible at either side of the cut.

My own continuity samples on the wide angle (3955.75, 3957.00, 3958.50, 3959.75) have gaps of 1.25-1.5 s. I did not re-grab the annotator's 3956.25-3959.00 samples because of the 8-frame budget. All the frames I checked are valid.
